dedupe_keys.name: homeland infrastructure foundation level data hifld open

description: HIFLD Open was the public tier of the Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data programme of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, run by its Geospatial Management Office to provide national, foundation-level geospatial data on United States infrastructure: several hundred layers such as power plants and transmission lines, cellular and broadcast towers, hospitals, LNG storage, airports, dams, bridges and schools, contributed by federal agencies including USACE, the Census Bureau, DOT, DOE, USGS, NOAA, EPA and the FCC, served as ArcGIS feature services and downloads in GeoJSON, Shapefile, CSV and file geodatabase. It has been decommissioned: the Federal Geographic Data Committee states that the HIFLD Open part of the programme has been decommissioned, and the former hub page now shows a not-found message. What remains at DHS is HIFLD Secure, which holds commercially licensed and for-official-use-only data on the DHS Geospatial Information Infrastructure and requires an account, an approved data use agreement and a homeland security mission. Copies of the public layers survive outside the government: SeerAI's HIFLD Archive on Source Cooperative (an archived copy of most layers, stating that public access ended on 25 August 2025) and a GitHub repository preserving 247 layers as GeoJSON with an index of 446 hub items; many layers also continue at the agencies that produced them. The layers were public domain or public use, varying by layer, and free. Caveats: the archives are third-party snapshots from 2025 that will not be updated, layers differ in vintage and completeness, and current versions must be sought from each source agency. The data serve hazard exposure, cascading failure, emergency response, resilience and network flow studies of United States infrastructure. No other catalogued records relate directly yet; the source-agency layers are candidates for their own records.

notes: Audit 2026-09-24: the official status was read on the FGDC HIFLD subcommittee page ('The HIFLD Open part of the program has been decommissioned'; subcommittee retired March 2026), the DHS GMO HIFLD page (last updated 2025-09-04; HIFLD Secure only; read with the page-fetch tool because the shell receives 403), the former hub page rendered in Chromium ('So sorry. We looked everywhere...'), the feature service directory (527 services, few HIFLD layers) and SeerAI's archive page. Corrections to round 1: the record described a live portal from a third-party mirror and set maturity unknown; HIFLD Open is decommissioned, so maturity is archived, the homepage is the DHS programme page, the archives are listed as third-party access routes and HIFLD Secure's restrictions are stated. The exact end date comes only from third parties (SeerAI: public access removed 2025-08-25; others give August or September 2025); DHS's crosswalk of layers to source agencies is reported by third parties and was not found on a DHS page. The hub page answers HTTP 200 and shows 'not found' only after its scripts run, so the link checker cannot detect it; it is marked dead by hand here. CISA's former HIFLD page returns Page Not Found.
